It does.

Terabyte drives were still just a pipe dream when Windows 98 was released.

Hitachi introduced the world's first one terabyte hard disk drive in 2007 (1 terabyte = 1,000 gigabytes)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terabyte#History

Windows 98 has a maximum hard drive capacity of 137 Gigabytes, and it looks like it won't be able to read all 137 GB either.

The 28 bit LBA supports 2^28 sectors which works out to 268435456 sectors. Each sector holds 512 bytes and therefore the maximum capacity is 137438953472 bytes.

This is the maximum Windows 98 supports for a bootable hard drive.

With SeaTools one can limit the capacity of certain hard drives and so I created a drive with exactly 268435456. This drive calculates to 128 MB capacity using Base 2 system, and after formatting is reported as a 127 MB drive by Windows. The BIOS POST summary shows it as a 136 GB drive.

https://www.philscomputerlab.com/windows-98-maximum-hard-drive-capacity.html#:~:text=127%20GB%20%2F%20128%20GB%20%2F%20137%20GB,Windows%2098%20supports%20for%20a%20bootable%20hard%20drive.
